{{short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Rolin-Louis Wavre''' (25 March 1896 in [[Canton of Neuchâtel|Neuchâtel]] – 9 December 1949 in [[Geneva]]) was a Swiss mathematician.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Tiercy, G.|title=Rolin Wavre|journal=Annales des l'Université de Lyon, Section A, Sciences de Mathématiques et Astronomie|volume=13|year=1950|pages=5–6}}</ref>

Wavre studied at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] and received his Ph.D. in 1921 from the [[University of Geneva]], where he became a professor extraordinarius in 1922, and a professor ordinarius in 1934 (as successor to Charles Cailler). Wavre did research on, among other subjects, logic and the philosophy of mathematics, in which he was an adherent of [[Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer|Brouwer]]'s intuitionism. Independently of, and almost simultaneously with, [[Leon Lichtenstein]], he dealt with equilibrium figures of a heterogeneous fluid mass, with a view to applications to planetary systems in astrophysics.

In 1932, in Zürich, he was a plenary speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] with talk ''L'aspect analytique du problème des figures planétaires''. He was an invited speaker at the ICM in 1920 in Strasbourg,<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1920/Main/icm1920.0308.0311.ocr.pdf|pages=308–311|year=1921|title=Compte rendu du Congrès international des mathématiciens tenu à Strasbourg du 22 au 30 Septembre 1920|chapter=''Un système d'equations a une infinité d'inconnues'' by R. Wavre}}</ref> in 1928 in Bologna,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wavre, R.|year=1929|title=Sur les figures d'équilibre d'une masse fluide hétérogène|journal=Atti del Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici: Bologna del 3 al 10 de settembre di 1928|pages=303–308}}</ref> and in 1936 in Oslo. For the two years 1936 and 1937, he was the president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]].

As an adolescent, Wavre attended Neuchâtel's gymnasium and was a close friend of [[Jean Piaget]] (who became a famous psychologist) and [[Gustave Juvet]] (who became a prominent mathematician).<ref>{{cite book|author=Vidal, Fernando|title=Piaget Before Piaget|year=1994|page=124|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6ESD-YzMyo4C&pg=PA124|isbn=9780674667167}}</ref>
